content: 1. Chronic inflammation can lead to increased levels of certain cytokines, which may alter the formation of CYP450 enzymes. Dupilumab has the potential to normalize the formation of these enzymes. When initiating or discontinuing dupilumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effects should be closely monitored. 2. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with duvelisib increases the area under the curve (AUC) of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing the risk of toxicities. Quinine also increases the levels or effects of duvelisib via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of quinine via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. 4. Eliglustat increases quinine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored, or the dosage of the P-gp substrate should be reduced and titrated to clinical effect. 5. Elranatamab increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Elranatamab can cause cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. This effect is more likely during the initiation of elranatamab step-up dosing and up to 14 days after the first treatment dose, as well as during and after CRS. 6. Eluxadoline increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, particularly when co-administering CYP3A substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 7. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. 8. Enasidenib decreases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Enasidenib, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce systemic exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. Dose adjustments of the substrate may be required based on clinical indications. 9. Encorafenib affects quinine levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Epcoritamab increases quinine levels by suppressing CYP enzyme activity through cytokine release. This suppression may lead to increased exposure to CYP substrates. Minimal changes in the concentration of certain CYP substrates can result in serious adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified as recommended in the substrate's prescribing information. 11. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Escitalopram and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ezogabine and quinine may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ezogabine has been associated with slight and transient QT prolongation, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 14. Fedratinib increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 15. Ferric maltol and quinine may increase each other's levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with certain oral medications may reduce the bioavailability of either ferric maltol or the oral drugs. Administration should be separated based on the absorption characteristics of the concomitant medication. 16. Quinine increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Serum potassium should be monitored during the initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Finerenone dosage should be adjusted as needed. 17. Flecainide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Flibanserin increases quinine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Quinine increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Floxuridine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Fluconazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Fluoxetine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Fluphenazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Formoterol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Foscarnet and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Quinine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 26. Gemifloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Gepirone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 28. Quinine increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases quinine levels via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Glofitamab increases quinine levels by suppressing CYP enzyme activity through cytokine release. This suppression may lead to increased exposure to CYP substrates. Minimal changes in the concentration of certain CYP substrates can result in serious adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified as recommended in the substrate's prescribing information. 30. Glycerol phenylbutyrate decreases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Glycerol phenylbutyrate is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor for decreased efficacy of CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 31. Guselkumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing guselkumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effects should be monitored. 32. Haloperidol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Ibutilide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Iloperidone increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both iloperidone and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Indacaterol (inhaled) and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 36. Indapamide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Quinine increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases quinine levels through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are advised. Isavuconazonium sulfate, a P-gp and CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of sensitive P-gp or CYP3A4 substrates, requiring dose adjustments. 38. Isoniazid increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Isradipine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Istradefylline increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Dose reduction of sensitive substrates may be necessary. 41. Itraconazole increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Ixekizumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing ixekizumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effects should be monitored. 43. Ketoconazole increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Lapatinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Quinine increases lemborexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 46. Lenacapavir increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 47. Letermovir increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Levofloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Levoketoconazole increases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Quinine increases lomitapide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lomitapide dosage should not exceed 30 mg/day. 51. Lonafarnib increases quinine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions if co-administered with P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce the P-gp substrate dose if needed. 52. Lonapegsomatropin decreases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Limited data suggest that growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated clearance. Caution is advised with sensitive CYP substrates. 53. Lopinavir and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Maprotiline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Mavorixafor and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. QTc should be monitored during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Quinine increases mavorixafor levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 56. Methadone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Quinine increases midazolam intranasal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with midazolam intranasal may increase systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 58. Mifepristone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be used if available. 59. Mitotane decreases quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer; monitoring is recommended when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates for possible dosage adjustments. 60. Moxifloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised.
